questions.question: Define the term 'margin of safety'. (2 marks)
A bottling plant has fixed costs of $36,000 a month and a variable cost of $3.60 a case. Calculate its total cost and its average cost at an output of 25,000 cases. (4 marks)
A bottling plant is launching a flavour that has never been sold in its region. Explain one difficulty it will face in forecasting sales of the new flavour. (4 marks)

A bottling plant sells at $6 a case with a variable cost of $3.60 a case and fixed costs of $36,000 a month. Calculate its break-even point, and calculate the new break-even point if the variable cost rises to $4. (4 marks)

A plant opens month 1 with $30,000. It expects receipts of $72,000, $120,000 and $129,600 and payments of $108,000, $122,400 and $108,000 over three months. Construct a cash-flow forecast showing net cash flow and the closing balance for each month. (4 marks)

A bottling plant budgets historically: each line is last year's actual figure adjusted for expected changes. Its finance manager has found a service contract for equipment sold two years ago, and proposes moving the whole firm to zero-based budgeting from next year. Assess whether the plant should do so. (10 marks)

A bottling plant sells at $6 a case, with a variable cost of $3.60 and fixed costs of $36,000 a month. It breaks even at 15,000 cases and currently produces 20,000. Its owner discounts heavily on orders above a hundred cases and is considering a second production line. Evaluate the usefulness of break-even analysis to the owner in making that decision. (20 marks)
